question: Is RVA 0x12CF3B0 in the installed MISERY Shipping image actually LoadPackage(const TCHAR*, ...), as ESC-02's mechanism field asserts?
verdict: NOT ESTABLISHED — no reproducible derivation exists; ESC-02's supporting claims are partly false; live P-04 call stopped before injection
method: Read-only static analysis of the installed image plus a repository-wide search for the derivation. The live process was never opened, not even for reading. No instrument under research/instruments/ipp/ was executed.

checks.name: repository search for the derivation
checks.observed: 0x12CF3B0 occurs only as an assertion in research/decisions.md (ESC-02) and in probe/controller code written from a prior session summary. No RESEARCH_LOG derivation entry exists.
checks.note: ESC-02's mechanism and thread_safety fields both cite an 'adjacent RESEARCH_LOG entry' that was never written.

checks.name: log-string anchors unique to LoadPackage(const TCHAR*)
strings_sought: LoadPackage: %s is a short script package name.
checks.observed: zero occurrences in either ASCII or UTF-16LE; load-path log/trace strings are stripped in this build (FlushAsyncLoading=0, LoadPackageAsync=0, IsShortPackageName=0, TryFromMountedName=0, 'SyncLoad - %s'=0)
checks.consequence: the standard 'string -> LEA xref -> enclosing function' identification route is unavailable in this build

checks.name: export table and PDB
checks.observed: 277 exports, all third-party GPU hints (AmdPowerXpressRequestHighPerformance, NvOptimusEnablement, D3D12SDKPath, agsDriverExtensions*). No engine exports. No LoadPackage export. Debug directory names MISERY-Win64-Shipping.pdb but no PDB ships anywhere under the install.
checks.falsifies: ESC-02's claim that LoadPackage is an 'exported CoreUObject function' is factually false for this monolithic Shipping build

checks.name: .pdata unwind table
checks.observed: 411385 RUNTIME_FUNCTION records; 0x12CF3B0 is an exact function begin, extent 0x12CF3B0-0x12CF65F, size 0x2AF
checks.note: proves a real function starts there; carries no name, so it constrains but cannot identify

checks.name: __FILE__ anchor for the translation unit
checks.observed: ANSI 'UObjectGlobals.cpp' present exactly once at file offset 0x5e88fa6 (VA 0x145e89da6), but zero lea r64,[rip+disp32] xrefs to it in .text
checks.note: UE stores __FILE__ pointers in static check-macro structures via relocation rather than an inline lea, so absence of lea xrefs is uninformative here — this test is neither positive nor negative

checks.name: prologue carried by the prior session summary
checks.summary_claimed_prologue: 4c8bf8488bda4489c44d8be9 (MOV R15,RCX; MOV RBX,RDX; MOV R12D,R8D; MOV R13,R9)
checks.note: the inherited prologue was wrong, which is what first exposed the missing derivation

what_is_not_in_doubt: process/build identity: the Shipping exe hashes byte-for-byte equal to build_key
the injection mechanism itself, proven separately in ESC-01
the asynchronous behaviour of the Zen loader (a claim about LoadPackage's behaviour, not its address)
what_is_in_doubt: exactly and only the identity of the call target address
consequence: research/instruments/ipp/p04_load_controller.py carries ADDRESS_IDENTITY_VERIFIED = False and refuses to inject until a real derivation lands in the same commit as its evidence
unblock_routes: A — Ghidra headless re-analysis of the current image with tracing from an identifiable anchor
B — transplant the signature from the symboled UnrealEditor-CoreUObject (PDB present for the same CL), correcting for configuration differences
C — change the mechanism to a target reachable by reflection (name-addressed) rather than by raw offset
